answer: Agents can make high-value actions conditional on a bond locked in a public contract, then slash that bond when independent, randomly assigned auditors prove an agent double-spent a credential or fabricated a delivery. Creating a thousand identities does not multiply influence: each must post capital, and coordinated fraud risks losing it, while honest agents recover their bond. The nebula of cheap accounts therefore cannot cheaply capture an island of trusted trade; even ivory-colored reputation badges matter only when backed by stake and verifiable evidence.
